microsd.title: Prepared microSD card
microsd.intro: A prepared card turns a compatible Raspberry Pi into a local library. It can serve its installed content without internet access. The supplied card determines the installed selection and capacity.
needs: A compatible Raspberry Pi, power supply and cooling. The tested reference is a Pi 4 Model B with 2 GB RAM.
A phone, tablet or computer with a browser. The built-in Wi-Fi is sufficient; an external USB radio is optional.
steps: With the Pi powered off, insert the supplied microSD card and connect power.
Join the DataArk hotspot. If your device reports no internet, choose to stay connected.
Open http://192.168.4.1/setup.html and enter the private setup code supplied with this card.
Choose separate caretaker and Linux admin passwords. Allow the first startup a few minutes.
hardware: Tested reference: Raspberry Pi 4 Model B, 2 GB RAM; CanaKit 3.5 A USB-C power supply; ventilated MazerPi case with fan and heatsinks.
A Pi 4 with 4 GB or 8 GB RAM provides more headroom. Use a reliable supply and cooling.

Optional range: a Linux-supported USB Wi-Fi adapter with external antenna and access-point support. Assign it to the hotspot under Wi-Fi or Hotspot / Wi-Fi adapter assignment; plugging it in alone does not change roles.

Optional storage: add an external USB content drive using System / Library / Use an external library drive. Existing content can be copied and verified before switching. Use adequate peripheral power.

appliance.title: Complete appliance
appliance.intro: A complete Data Ark includes its host and prepared system storage, with either an external library drive or a system-drive library. Installed content needs no internet connection.
needs: The supplied host, system storage, power supply and any supplied library drive.
A browser device on the hotspot or the same local network.
steps: Connect the supplied library drive, if any, before applying power.
For a hotspot appliance, join its supplied Wi-Fi network and open http://192.168.4.1/setup.html.
For a LAN appliance, connect it and your browser to the same local network; use the device address supplied with it.
If first-owner setup is pending, enter the supplied private code and choose the two passwords. If the owner already set credentials locally, no additional code step is needed.
hardware: Keep the supplied storage attached while the appliance is running.
Use System / System / Power to restart or shut down safely. A shutdown requires someone to power the device back on.

content-drive.title: Content drive / split Ark
content-drive.intro: A library drive carries public content, configuration and the recovery kit. It can help rebuild a replacement host. A surviving host can prepare replacement library media. A content drive alone is not a bootable operating system.
needs: A supported running Linux host with administrative access and an attached library drive.
Internet for missing operating-system packages and software dependencies. Existing public content is reused.
steps: Attach the library drive. Locate its DATA-ARK-CONFIG folder and included recovery kit; follow its README rather than executing an arbitrary script from unknown media.
Preview the bootstrap/recovery plan on the new host and select the intended library location.
Run the supported installation workflow with Linux administrative authorization. Set owner credentials locally when offered.
Verify library readers and content. When preparing a second Ark for someone else, use Make another Ark / Prepare for a new owner to establish a fresh identity and private setup code.
hardware: Never reuse the original owner credentials or printed setup code for a new recipient.
When starting with configuration but no content, choose a capacity-appropriate restore preset; downloads need an upstream connection.

bootstrap.title: Software / bootstrap kit
bootstrap.intro: The downloadable kit supplies software and public collection configuration. You supply the host and storage. It is not a complete operating-system image and does not include the public collection.
needs: A supported Linux installation, administrative access, storage and internet for installation.
The verified bootstrap kit and its matching README.
steps: Download the kit and checksum from the DEJ Software bootstrap page or the Ark's DEJ Software collection.
Extract the kit onto a formatted content drive or the installation location described by its README.
Review the preview, select the platform profile and library location, then complete installation with local administrative authorization.
Set credentials in the trusted installer. If you deliberately defer first-owner setup to a browser, prepare a unique code and supply it privately before exposing that setup page.
hardware: Original Raspberry Pi provides the optional hotspot appliance profile. LAN-only Debian hosts serve an existing wired or Wi-Fi network.
Content acquisition is separate from installing the software; choose only the collections that fit.

linux-lan.title: Linux LAN server
linux-lan.intro: A Data Ark can serve an existing local network from a supported Linux server or laptop. A Wi-Fi access point is optional, and a Pi is not required for this profile.
needs: A supported Debian-based host, administrative access and an existing wired or Wi-Fi network.
Library storage and internet for installation dependencies.
steps: Use the supported bootstrap workflow and select the LAN profile. Preserve the host's existing network configuration.
Choose a library location or attach an existing content drive. Set the caretaker password through the trusted local installer.
Open the host's LAN address in a browser and check the dashboard, Help and installed readers.
Use the host's existing Linux account credentials for SSH. There is no extra activation code after owner credentials have been established.
hardware: A LAN server does not need a hotspot, a second Wi-Fi adapter or Raspberry Pi-specific hardware.
If ownership is handed to someone else with browser setup deferred, generate a fresh private pairing code through recipient preparation.

docker.title: Docker / container
docker.intro: The container serves a library on an existing local network using host-mounted media and persistent state. It does not manage the host's radios, disks, root account or power.
needs: Docker Engine or Docker Desktop with Compose.
An existing library folder, a writable public configuration folder and persistent private/state volumes.
steps: Follow the Container guide. Set ARK_MEDIA, ARK_CONFIGURATION and ARK_PORT in the supplied Compose environment file.
Build or select the reviewed image, then start it using the documented Compose command. Building needs internet; reading installed content does not.
Set the caretaker password using the documented caretaker-password command in the host terminal. No first-owner pairing code or Linux admin password is created by the container.
Open the host address and selected port in a browser. Keep the same media/configuration mounts and private/state volumes when recreating or updating it.
hardware: Networking, physical drives, host credentials, power and optional HTTPS are host responsibilities.
Do not delete the private/state volumes when you intend to preserve passwords, posts, banner and operational state.
